paper_metadata.title: Explicit block-encoding for partial differential equation-constrained optimization

summary: This paper proposes a fully coherent gate-based quantum algorithm for PDE-constrained optimization by combining LCHS-based forward simulation with quantum Hamiltonian descent and explicit block-encoding of the objective. It reports two simulated examples: a Black-Scholes volatility calibration instance using 19 qubits and a 1D wave-equation material-design instance using 12 qubits, with asymptotic claims of polynomial speedup in N and T and exponential speedup in spatial dimension d under strong convexity.

experiments.description: Fully coherent gate-based quantum algorithm for PDE-constrained optimization, demonstrated on a Black-Scholes parameter calibration problem using block-encoding of the objective and quantum Hamiltonian descent with product-formula time evolution.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Hamiltonian descent (QHD) with block-encoded objective and product-formula simulation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Empirical optimization run for a fixed number of iterations/time steps; in the Black-Scholes example, Nstep = 1000
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Uniform superposition over discretized design variables; initial state prepared by Hadamard gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Volatility parameter sigma is discretized with 4 qubits; objective is encoded via block-encoding of the PDE solution-dependent error objective Ferr
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_{xi in [0,1]} Ferr(xi) = ||u(x,T;xi) - u_ref||^2 subject to Black-Scholes PDE constraints and sigma^2 = (sigma_max^2 - sigma_min^2) xi + sigma_min^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: PDE constraint handled by forward quantum simulation; objective encoded coherently via block-encoding
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(s) = (1/(2 lambda(s))) Lambda^(M) + lambda(s) F_hat, with lambda(s)=e^{nu s}

problem_instance.description: Black-Scholes call option volatility calibration from a reference option price

dataset_specification.description: Call option with strike K=30, maturity T=1, risk-free rate r=0.02; reference price generated from analytical Black-Scholes formula at sigma=0.3

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Domain truncated to x in [ln(1e-4), ln(10K)] and discretized into 64 nodes; reference state prepared from analytical European call option price at x_ref closest to ln(Ke^{-r})
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Statevector simulation used to validate block-encoding; product-formula time evolution used to test optimization; objective history and probability distributions reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Analytical Black-Scholes solution used to generate reference data; mean objective value bar_F estimated from all parameters
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of computational basis to obtain optimized design variable; objective expectation and standard deviation tracked

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: objective expectation decreases toward optimum with decreasing variance

classical_baselines.method_name: classical forward simulation with adjoint-variable optimization
classical forward simulation with p-th order time integrator

classical_baselines.value: O(MNT + alpha_PDE^(1+1/p) d^(1+1/p) N^((eta/d)(1+1/p+d/eta)) T^(1+1/p) epsilon^(-1/p))

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in system size N; exponential speedup in spatial dimension d; polynomial speedup in evolution time T
speedup_claims.baseline_method: conventional classical PDE-constrained optimization with adjoint-variable method
speedup_claims.conditions: regime N >> M, strongly convex objective, fault-tolerant gate-based quantum computer, using underlying quantum PDE solver speedups
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is inherited from the forward PDE solver; end-to-end guarantee is derived only under strong convexity. The numerical experiment uses statevector simulation and product-formula evolution, not a real QPU.

speedup_claims.factor: block-encoding objective cost ~ O(alpha_PDE d N^(eta/d) M^2 m T log(1/epsilon)^(1/beta))
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical objective evaluation via forward simulation
speedup_claims.conditions: interaction-picture simulation with LCHS-based forward solver
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an asymptotic query/gate complexity expression, not an empirical runtime.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ~O(alpha_PDE d N^(eta/d) M^3 T / (h_x^2 epsilon)) for the full algorithm under strong convexity; block-encoding objective function cost ~O(alpha_PDE d N^(eta/d) M^2 m T log(1/epsilon)^(1/beta))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: ~O(M N T log(1/epsilon) + alpha_PDE^(1+1/p) d^(1+1/p) N^(eta/d (1+1/p + d/eta)) T^(1+1/p) / epsilon^(1/p))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault-tolerant quantum computer with sufficiently low logical error rates; the paper's claimed speedup is asymptotic and inherited from the underlying PDE solver, not demonstrated on hardware.
limiting_factors: Only statevector simulation and product-formula emulation are reported
Objective is a toy-sized Black-Scholes calibration instance with 19 qubits
Speedup depends on strong convexity and asymptotic PDE-solver assumptions
Block-encoding and interaction-picture simulation overheads are substantial

experiments.description: Fully coherent gate-based quantum algorithm for PDE-constrained optimization, demonstrated on a one-dimensional wave-equation material-parameter design problem using block-encoding and quantum Hamiltonian descent with product-formula time evolution.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Hamiltonian descent (QHD) with block-encoded objective and product-formula simulation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Empirical optimization run for a fixed number of iterations/time steps; in the wave-equation example, Nstep = 100
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Uniform superposition over discretized design variables; initial state prepared by Hadamard gates

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: xi1, xi2 in [0,1] via 3-bit discretization each

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two design variables xi1 and xi2 are discretized with 3 qubits each; objective is encoded coherently as a maximization problem by using the sign-flipped reflection operator
problem_formulation.objective_function: max_{xi in [0,1]^2} integral_{3W/4}^{W} [ c(x)^2 w(x,T)^2 + (partial_t w(x,T))^2 ] dx subject to the 1D wave equation and piecewise-constant speed profile c(x)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: PDE constraint handled by forward quantum simulation; maximization converted to minimization by adding a minus sign to the objective function / replacing RP with -RP
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(s) = (1/(2 lambda(s))) Lambda^(M) + lambda(s) F_hat, with lambda(s)=e^{nu s}

problem_instance.description: Material parameter design for a 1D wave equation to maximize energy concentration in a target region

dataset_specification.description: Domain length W=2^5-1, simulation time T=48, piecewise wave speed c(x) with two design variables over intermediate segments

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Spatial domain discretized with 5 qubits; initial velocity sparse and prepared by amplitude encoding; design variables discretized with 3 qubits each
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Statevector simulation used to validate block-encoding; product-formula time evolution used to test optimization; objective history and probability distributions reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Mean objective value bar_F estimated from all parameters; initial state prepared by amplitude encoding for sparse initial velocity
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of computational basis to obtain optimized design variables; objective expectation and standard deviation tracked

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: objective expectation increases toward optimum with decreasing variance

classical_baselines.method_name: classical forward simulation with Hamiltonian simulation and expectation evaluation

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in system size N; exponential speedup in spatial dimension d; polynomial speedup in evolution time T
speedup_claims.baseline_method: conventional classical PDE-constrained optimization with adjoint-variable method
speedup_claims.conditions: regime N >> M, strongly convex objective, fault-tolerant gate-based quantum computer, using underlying quantum PDE solver speedups
speedup_claims.caveats: The numerical experiment is a statevector simulation with product-formula evolution; no hardware execution or measured runtime advantage is reported.

speedup_claims.factor: block-encoding objective cost ~ O(alpha_PDE d N^(eta/d) M^2 m T log(1/epsilon)^(1/beta))
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical objective evaluation via forward simulation
speedup_claims.conditions: simple implementation using Hamiltonian simulation oracles for anti-Hermitian coefficient matrices
speedup_claims.caveats: Asymptotic expression only; no empirical gate counts are reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ~O(alpha_PDE d N^(eta/d) M^3 T / (h_x^2 epsilon)) for the full algorithm under strong convexity; block-encoding objective function cost ~O(alpha_PDE d N^(eta/d) M^2 m T log(1/epsilon)^(1/beta))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: ~O(M N T log(1/epsilon) + alpha_PDE^(1+1/p) d^(1+1/p) N^(eta/d (1+1/p + d/eta)) T^(1+1/p) / epsilon^(1/p))
